restoration_note: This teaching describes the cosmic architecture of three concentric Zones built by the Living Spirit: innermost = the five powers of Darkness (males/females); middle = the Five Sons of the First Man fettering the enmity; outermost = the firmament-Zone presided over by the great King of Honor / Great Builder. The well-preserved opening (lines 1–9) and the recovered titles (King of Honor at line 14) constrain the editorial fills strongly. Restorations confirmed include the chapter numeral, line-break completions of ⲍⲱⲛⲏ / ⲡⲣⲱⲙⲉ / ⲥⲧⲉⲣⲉⲱⲙⲁ / ⲉⲧϣⲟⲟⲡ, the parallel ⲉⲡⲉⲓⲁⲏ converter, the ⲛ̄ⲕⲉⲕⲁⲩⲉ idiom, the Living Spirit title at {3}, and the King of Honor title at {15}. Lines 11–13 and 15 contain mid-clause lacunae of 4–11 characters whose specific lexical content (the prepositional phrases governing 'upon him,' 'after him,' the 8-char fill after ⲡϣ in line 13, and the 11-char fill in line 15) cannot be safely reconstructed from the surviving traces and are left unrestored.

restorations.basis: Chapter numeral confirmed by flanking ⲗ̄ⲍ at the title and end-marker.
Line-break completion of ⲍⲱⲛ-ⲏ; immediately followed by ⲏ.
Line-break completion of ⲡⲣⲱ-ⲙⲉ from line 7's ⲙ̄ⲡⲣⲱ.

The 'five sons of the ___' standardly refers to the Five Sons of the Living Spirit (Splenditenens/King of Honor/Adamas/King of Glory/Omophoros), the cosmic architects who occupy the third Zone. Living Spirit is named at line 2 as the builder, and the partial ⲙⲡⲡ continues with ⲡⲛⲁ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄. Lexicon: ⲡⲡⲛⲁ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄.
Parallel to line 8's ⲉⲡⲉⲓⲁⲏ ⲉⲣⲉ... circumstantial construction; immediately followed by ⲉⲣⲉ + nominal subject ⲡⲕⲱⲧ.
Pre-nominal circumstantial converter ⲉⲣⲉ before ⲡⲕⲱⲧ ⲧⲏⲣϩ.

6-char gap after ⲉϩϫ (= ⲉϫⲛ̄). Could be ⲉϩϫⲱϥ alone plus start of next phrase, or ⲉϩϫⲛ̄ + a noun (the firmament / the great one). The English 'upon{6}' breaks ambiguously and the specific governing noun cannot be determined from traces.

10-char gap ending in -ⲧⲙⲉ before ⲁⲣⲁϩ (=ⲉⲣⲟϥ 'to him'). Editor's tentative 'ⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ' (the Hearing) does not fit the English 'him, also other (things)...' context. No spiritually constrained word ending in -ⲧⲙⲉ fits the local syntax securely.
Standard idiom ⲛ̄ⲕⲉⲕⲁⲩⲉ 'and other things'; ⲛ̄ⲕⲉ- is the visible prefix.
4-char gap at end of line with no surviving traces or constraining context.
9-char gap before ⲛⲥⲱⲩ (=ⲛ̄ⲥⲱϥ 'after him'). The verbal element governing 'after him' is unconstrained — could be a verb of motion, gathering, or attachment.
5-char gap as object of ⲁϩⲉⲓ ϣⲁ 'he hung'. Could be ⲡⲕⲱⲧ, ⲡⲧⲏⲣϥ̄, or another item — not securely constrained.
Greek loanword ⲥⲧⲉⲣⲉⲱⲙⲁ 'firmament' visible from -ⲉⲣⲉⲱⲙⲁ; the firmament-Zone is the third Zone of the reading (Lexicon: firmament = ⲛ̄ⲥⲧⲉⲣⲉⲱⲙⲁ).
8-char gap with only ϣ visible. 'Above ϣ...' could yield several readings (ϣⲁⲛⲧⲉ-, ϣⲏⲩⲉ, etc.) — not constrained.
Subject 'which is in a Zone — is the great King of Honor' fits the third/outermost Zone of the architecture. Feminine ⲧⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧⲉ matches gender of ⲍⲱⲛⲏ and approximate length (~9 chars).
Reading identifies the firmament-Zone occupant as the King of Honor (ⲡⲛⲁⲃ ⲛ̄ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ ⲡⲧⲁⲓⲟ), the ruling Divine Truth governing the heavens of the natural; ⲡⲛⲁⲟ̄ ⲛ̄ already visible.
Completion of ⲉⲧϣⲟⲟⲡ 'who exists' from visible ⲉⲧϣ-.
11-char gap after 'who exists' before 'within the cosmos'. The qualifying clause/phrase (e.g., 'over all,' 'in glory,' 'as the great one') cannot be securely reconstructed.
Partial ⲙⲡⲕ + 7 chars; ⲙ̄ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ ⲧⲏⲣϥ̄ 'of the whole cosmos' fits length and matches the closing summary in line 16 (ⲙ̄ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ).
Single character preceding ⲧⲉ ⲙ̄ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ ('is of the cosmos'). Most likely the final letter of feminine ⲧⲍⲱⲛⲏ closing the chapter's summary statement '[this is] the (third) Zone of the cosmos.'
